stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its velocity at time t seconds is \( v(t) = - 2 t^{3} + 2 t^{2} + 2 t + 28 \) meters per second, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 3, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 2 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( v(3) = -2 \) and \( a(3) = -40 \) have the same sign.

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = - 6 t^{2} + 4 t + 2 \), so \( a(3) = -40 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(3)\right| = 2 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(3) = -2 \) and \( a(3) = -40 \) have the same sign, the speed of the particle is increasing at t = 3.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign
